title: Cap. IV open: general decree urged as Scriptural — Resp. ad articulos, Hippolytus, Hague Remonstrants
pass_a_gloss: But it is worthy of observation that that prior general decree, which designates no one singularly to salvation, is nonetheless urged most by Arminius, and thrust forward for that predestination which sacred Scripture has commended to us. So in his Response to the articles, article 4: This decree (he speaks of that general and indeterminate one) I say is the foundation of Christianity, of salvation, and of certainty concerning salvation; and that concerning it one treats at Rom. 8, 10, 11, and in the first chapter to the Ephesians. He teaches the same plainly in the Letter to Hippolytus, in which he skips over that predestination by which God is said to have decreed to save certain singular persons and gift them with faith, as a matter of small moment, and least founded in the sacred Scriptures. But the Remonstrants in the Hague Conference, plainly forgetful of any particular decree whatsoever, so direct their arguments as to prove that this sole decree, by which God indiscriminately established that he wills to save any persevering in faith, but to pour out wrath upon all the unbelieving, is the whole and entire decree of Predestination, p. 62.
pass_b_english: Note well: that prior general decree, which names no one singularly to salvation, is what Arminius most urges and thrusts forward as the predestination Scripture recommends. So in his Response to the articles, art. 4: This decree (the general, indeterminate one) I say is the foundation of Christianity, salvation, and certainty of salvation; and Rom. 8, 10, 11 and Ephesians 1 treat of it. The same in his Letter to Hippolytus, where he skips the predestination by which God decreed to save certain singular persons and gift them faith — as a small matter, scarcely founded in Scripture. The Remonstrants at the Hague Conference, forgetting any particular decree, aim to prove this sole decree — God indiscriminately wills to save any who persevere in faith and pour wrath on all unbelievers — is the whole and entire decree of Predestination (p. 62).
source_text: Est autem observatu dignum, prius illud generale decretum, quod neminem singulariter ad salutem designat, urgeri tamen maxime ab Arminio, et obtrudi pro illa praedestinatione, quam sacra Scriptura nobis commendavit. Sic in Responsione sua ad articulos, artic. 4. Hoc decretum (loquitur de isto generali et indeterminato) dico esse fundamentum Christianismi, salutis, et certitudinis de salute; deque illo agi ad Rom. 8, 10, 11. et primo capite ad Ephesios. Idem plane docet in Epistola ad Hippolytum, in qua illam praedestinationem, qua Deus dicitur decrevisse singulares quasdam personas salvare et fide donare, quasi rem parvi momenti, et in sacris Scripturis minime fundatam, transilit. Remonstrantes autem in Collatione Hagiensi, plane immemores particularis cujuscunque decreti, eo dirigunt argumenta sua, ut probent hoc unicum decretum, quo Deus indiscriminatim statuit, velle se quoslibet in fide perseverantes servare, iram vero super omnibus incredulis effundere, esse totum et integrum decretum Praedestinationis, pag. 62.
